kinds.about: Texture replacements: one folder per game serial (e.g. SLUS-20312) holding replacements/ with the pack's files in any subfolders, as PCSX2's textures/<serial>/replacements.
kinds.doc: PCSX2 v2.6.3 reads <Textures>/<serial>/replacements recursively (GSTextureReplacements.cpp:262-265, 395-431), Textures being the profile's relative textures folder in its data root, and follows links (FileSystem.cpp:2114-2120); it creates <serial>/dumps and replacements only while dumping (:270-286), which Semu never turns on. LoadTextureReplacements is on only while a pack is installed, asynchronous, and never precached (Pcsx2Config.cpp:774-776).

mods.doc: Dormant until a pack is placed: the library is <paths.mods>/pcsx2/textures/<serial>, one link per game folder into ${state_root}/config/PCSX2/textures.

doc.runtime: Linux executes the pinned, source-built PCSX2 package, carrying semu_render_hook.patch, from the bundle asset root.
doc.state: PCSX2 2.6.3 reads $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/PCSX2; Semu maps that to the per-emulator state root. Settings, memory cards, save states, snapshots, cache, logs, and textures remain Semu-owned generated/runtime state.
doc.graphics: [EmuCore/GS] Renderer = 12 forces OpenGL in the generated profile. The source-built package carries semu_render_hook.patch: GSDeviceOGL publishes the presented frame to libsemurenderer (ABI 3) after the final upright present draw, then runs the post-UI pass after PCSX2's ImGui immediately before the emulator-owned swap.
doc.firmware: The configured PS2 BIOS directory is read in place; Semu never writes ROM, BIOS or external emulation roots.
doc.input: The packaged Game Mode process binds Pad1 to its first SDL gamepad, SDL-0. The profile compiler reads this Linux platform declaration directly; it does not inherit a stale host enumeration index.
doc.platforms: PCSX2 is intentionally Linux-only until a reproducible source-built Darwin slice exists. An upstream application archive is not a production fallback.
doc.playlist: PCSX2 2.6.3 has no .m3u reader: IsDiscFileName lists no m3u, so it takes a playlist for an ISO image, fails to identify it and quits in -batch. Semu passes the playlist's first disc after -- (playlist.open first_entry). The pause menu (OpenPauseMenu, Ctrl+M) has Change Disc, whose file selector opens in that disc's folder, where the other discs sit.
doc.content: What PCSX2 bc8151d2 boots: its disc names (pcsx2/VMManager.cpp:2382), .elf (2361) and block dumps (2366); any other file is read as a flat ISO (1236), which is how a Nero .nrg boots (pcsx2/CDVD/InputIsoFile.cpp:296-301 detects Nero offsets). No .m3u and no archive: Semu opens playlists for it (playlist.open first_entry).

save_states.doc: PCSX2 cycles ten slots shown as 1-10 and wraps both ways (pcsx2/ImGui/ImGuiOverlays.cpp:1162-1186 at bc8151d, VMManager.h:69); every VM start selects slot 1 (ImGuiOverlays.cpp:1125, 1377).

menu.doc: Seen 2026-10-03 in the podman VM (tests/integration/menu-pause.sh with openbox, Marvel vs. Capcom 2 through the render hook on llvmpipe): Ctrl+P (TogglePause) froze the game under PCSX2's own Paused notice, and a menu record written while paused stayed invisible until Ctrl+P resumed it, so a paused PCSX2 stops presenting. The Semu menu therefore opens over the running game, and on Linux it holds the pad while it is open (EVIOCGRAB once every pad is at rest, released after the closing press), so the game sees none of the menu's input; taps and Steam's radial keys still reach it.
